page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.large is an entry-tier general purpose virtual server instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core across 2 threads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz, the x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AES, BMI2, and FMA. System memory totals 8.0 GB RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation ratio.

The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached cloud disks for persistent filesystem volumes. Network throughput is bounded by a baseline bandwidth limit of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated hardware GPUs are provided.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the constraints of a single physical core configuration. Single-core compute capability is modest, recording a stress-ng score of 1099.38 and a Geekbench single-core score of 937.0. Multi-core execution demonstrates limited scaling given the dual-thread topology on one physical core, with stress-ng reaching 1456.5 and Geekbench reaching 1108.0. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register 10.45 GB/sec for read and 9.47 GB/sec for write operations, positioning memory access speeds in the lower performance brackets across comparative workloads.

Throughput measurements include 1.48 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 1.26 GB/sec for static web serving. Natural language generation using a compact 135M model generates 38.09 tokens per second. Given its balanced resource footprint and entry-level compute threshold, this instance provides cost efficiency for low-traffic microservices, non-critical background jobs, lightweight staging environments, and basic utility services.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5ne.large is a general purpose instance delivering a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory configuration. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, backed by 8.0 GB of system memory. The architecture supports hardware virtualization via KVM, alongside AVX-512 and AES vector instruction sets. The server includes no bundled local storage and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth cap. Benchmark testing reflects entry-level throughput, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1108.0 and large-block memory read speeds of 10.45 GB/sec. Given its shared-core execution model and resource density, the instance offers cost-efficient capacity for lightweight tasks such as staging environments, basic internal microservices, and secondary utility workloads.
